artifacts.summary: 5-phase plan fixing the missing task-lookup-lib.sh fixture entry, the lint check_emit_perline variable-redirect false positive, new lint regression coverage, two dormant audit-gap fixtures, and full shellcheck/redeploy verification.

memory_candidates.content: In this repo's core shell test suites, fixtures that build a minimal .claude/scripts tree from an EXPLICIT lib name list are a recurring breakage class: when a production script (e.g. task-lock.sh) gains a new unconditional `source lib/<new>.sh`, every explicit-list fixture that copies that script silently loses it and fails at load time, while wholesale `lib/*.sh` copy fixtures are immune by construction. Audit approach that worked: classify each candidate suite into five buckets -- wholesale copy (safe), explicit list already complete, no fixture copy at all (script sourced from its real location), static-analysis-only (bash -n/grep, never executed), and genuine gap. Note that many lib lists span shell continuation lines, so a naive single-line grep under-reports both completeness and gaps. Gaps can be dormant rather than red (e.g. a suite that only ever runs the SUT with --dry-run never reaches the subprocess that sources the missing lib), so redness is not a reliable detector -- structural audit is.
